title: Effects of strength, explosive and plyometric training on energy cost of running in ultra-endurance athletes
authors: Giovanelli N, Taboga P, Rejc E, Lazzer S
population: Well-trained male ultra-marathoners (38.2 +/- 7.1 years; VO2max 55.4 +/- 4.0 ml/kg/min); 25 runners divided into exercise (n=13) and control (n=12) groups; randomization is not stated in the abstract
findings: A 12-week home-based strength, explosive and plyometric (SEP) program lowered the energy cost of running at all four tested speeds: -6.4% at 8 km/h, -3.5% at 10, -4.0% at 12 and -3.2% at 14 km/h (p < 0.05); the control group showed no differences.
Contact time increased at 8, 10 and 12 km/h (mean +4.4%).
Changes in energy cost were inversely related to changes in maximal lower-limb muscle power at 10 km/h (r = -0.67) and 12 km/h (r = -0.86).
Authors suggest adding at least three SEP sessions per week to normal endurance training may decrease the cost of running.
limitations: Small, male-only sample; randomization not stated; no race-performance or injury outcome; economy measured at 8-14 km/h only; the three-sessions-per-week suggestion was not tested against other frequencies.
implications: For ultra and trail plans, include a strength/explosive/plyometric block of about 12 weeks; gains were largest at the slowest tested speed (8 km/h).
A home-based program was effective, supporting an equipment-light option.
Use 2 sessions per week at high mileage and flag the authors' 3 per week as optional, because the dose is untested.

verification.notes: Reclassified from rct to other (controlled trial): abstract says runners were 'divided into' groups. Removed the unsupported 'control group not randomization-blind' limitation. Participants are ultra-marathoners, not 100-mile runners.
